title: flowmap is ready to publish as an Apache 2.0 repo
intent: Prepare the repo to be made public, so the plugin installs on any machine without GitHub credentials, and people can find and use flowmap and the Fjall deploy behind it.
delta: No flow, step, symbol or call edge moves: the CLI is untouched. The repo gains an Apache 2.0 license, loses the GitHub Pages workflow that the hosted viewer replaced in PR #5, and loses the agent planning notes. The README gets setup steps for a new machine that assume a public repo. Making the repo public is a separate step, done by hand in GitHub settings.

chapters.title: flowmap is licensed Apache 2.0
chapters.before: No license: a public repo would be readable, but nobody could legally use, copy or change it.
chapters.after: LICENSE holds the unmodified Apache 2.0 text from apache.org. plugin.json declares `"license": "Apache-2.0"` and the repository URL, and the README ends with a License section.
chapters.claim: Anyone can use, change and ship flowmap, with an explicit patent grant.
chapters.why: This decides whether someone who finds the repo can adopt it at work. Apache 2.0's patent grant is what company legal teams usually ask for.

questions.q: Should flowmap also ship a NOTICE file, which Apache 2.0 asks redistributors to carry forward?
questions.why: Only matters if you want attribution to travel with forks.

questions.q: Does `claude plugin validate .` still pass with the new `license` and `repository` fields in plugin.json?
questions.why: An invalid manifest stops the plugin from installing.

chapters.title: A new machine installs the plugin with two commands
chapters.before: The README covered `/plugin install` but not what a second machine needs, and with a private repo every install needed stored GitHub credentials.
chapters.after: An 'On a new machine' section lists Python 3.11+ and git, the two `/plugin` commands, `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_PREFER_HTTPS=1` for machines without a GitHub SSH key, how to put `bin/` on the shell PATH, and how updates arrive: only when `version` in plugin.json changes.
chapters.claim: Once the repo is public, setup needs no GitHub login.
chapters.why: Until the repo is public, these steps fail without credentials. Merge this when you flip the visibility.

questions.q: plugin.json pins `version` at 0.1.0, so installed plugins never pick up new commits. Bump it on each release, or remove it so installs follow commits?
questions.why: Decides whether the work machine ever gets fixes without a reinstall.

chapters.title: The GitHub Pages publisher and the planning notes are gone
chapters.before: `.github/workflows/flowmap-pages.yml` pushed change pages to a `gh-pages` branch that nothing linked to, and Pages was never turned on. The plan for PR #4 sat in `docs/superpowers/plans/`.
chapters.after: The workflow is deleted (the `gh-pages` branch is deleted on the remote too). The plan is deleted, and `/docs/superpowers/` is gitignored so later agent plans stay local.
chapters.claim: Nothing public points at a dead publishing path.
chapters.why: In a public repo, Pages would start working and serve stale pages next to the hosted viewer.

questions.q: The deleted plan is still in the history of PR #4. Is that acceptable in a public repo?
questions.why: Removing it from history means rewriting main and losing the PR refs.
